doc.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Playing and recording with Jon Lucien, who helps with his album
summary: Lucien befriends him, invites him to Puerto Rico, hires him as percussionist and helps him put his analog tapes into digital form.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: in that embrace. And he, after, he said, “So what you do my son?” I said, “Well I’m a musician, I’m a percussionist” etcetera. He says, “Well look,” he gave me his card. He said “I’m going back to” he was living in Puerto Rico at the time and he says, “I’m going back in three days. Call me.” I said okay. In three days I called Jon. From that day anytime Jon came to New York he would call me and I would go and pick him up at the airport. I would carry his guitar. I would carry his guitar. Through Jon, he and Herbie Hancock came off the plane together. I didn’t know these guys were buddies. He, Wayne Shorter and Herbie Hancock were like this you know. And man, I carried Jon’s guitar — when we were pregnant with our first child I remember being on the phone and I said to Jon I was like, “Jon” I said, “the only thing I really want to give that baby right now is the waves of the ocean.” Jon says, “Come, come to Puerto Rico. Come and stay with us.” So I packed my wife up, packed our bags and we went and stayed with Jon in Puerto Rico and it was there just with him playing the music and stuff, and me knocking around on a couple of instruments he had around the place. He says, “Man, I want you to start playing with me. Come and play with me my son.” And that’s — the rest was history. I was on the bandstand with Jon, recording with Jon, gigging with Jon, traveling with Jon, Jon appeared, a little cameo appearance on my CD on “Island Woman” you will hear him in the back of me [scats]. Ah. Just that he would breathe on my album was — and as a matter of fact I had stopped playing music altogether. And when I took my tape to Jon, you know I had a cassette tape and I had never done anything with what I had recorded. I took it to Jon and Jon said, “My son, but you have something here. You’ve got to do something with this” you know. And it was Jon who took me by the hand, Monk, by the hand, into the studio with my two inch, my two boxes of two inch analog tapes.
I have three in my basement.
